source_atoms.finding: agentZero is an exported running-state/evidence surface; code/, cognition/, state/, pulse/ and tests are separated from research interpretation. Export description is provenance, not proof that every current component is live now.
AutonomyPulse is bound as one asyncio task to the existing application lifecycle; it explicitly creates no second server.

Each pulse checks canonical user/session/runtime attestation, rejects an active canonical turn, obtains exactly one planner step, reserves a one-shot dispatch, then injects only the nonce into the existing managed terminal. Unknown failures remain explicit PULSE_BLOCKED and acquire no completion credit.
Dispatch uses a session-scoped lease with random nonce, TTL, exact goal_id/step_id/generation/instruction payload and atomic consume/delete; stale generation or drifted admitted step fails closed.

Model planning output is constrained to canonical JSON with reason|effect|complete_candidate. Model output cannot prove completion; complete_candidate only invokes independent controller verification. Effect proposals remain bounded and are admitted by deterministic code.

AutonomyController declares model proposals are never evidence; goal state includes bounded budgets, typed step kinds, generation, completion contract and effect evidence. Current controller supports wait only with a typed registered wake_condition, while the current planner intentionally does not allow model-emitted wait decisions.

One-shot dispatch is atomically bound into turn provenance; Stop re-enters the exact autonomous goal/step/generation, compiles reason output through AutonomyPlanner, and treats an unexecuted effect step as failure. Human preemption reconciles without replaying an effect or inventing success.

forensic_conclusions.claim: The strongest reusable AgentZero mechanism is a deterministic local deliberation loop around model cognition: durable goal/step state -> one-shot dispatch -> bounded model candidate -> exact Stop/result re-entry -> deterministic transition/completion verification.
The inspected AgentZero autonomy lane is not evidence of native child/subagent spawning. It drives one existing managed model terminal and does not provide a child actor/task lifecycle ABI.

A useful architectural split already exists: the deterministic controller can represent WAIT only with a typed wake condition, while free model planner output cannot emit WAIT. Frankenstein-2.0 should preserve this separation rather than allowing text such as 'wait' to stall a workpackage.

The session-scoped one-dispatch-at-a-time mechanism is suitable for a single local agent loop but would over-serialize GRID if transplanted unchanged. GRID requires workpackage/invocation-scoped leases and immutable WorkExecutionBinding rather than one global session lane.

frankenstein2_grid_successor.name: GRIDLocalDeliberation/v1
frankenstein2_grid_successor.purpose: Preserve AgentZero's deterministic cognition envelope while allowing bounded parallel candidate work under GRID without creating a second state authority.
required_invariants: model output is candidate cognition, never evidence or completion authority
every candidate binds workpackage_id + execution binding + generation + source context digest
lease scope is per workpackage/invocation, not a single mutable session pointer
parallel cells may propose; deterministic arbitration admits at most the allowed transition set
EffectRequestCandidate must traverse typed EffectDecision authority before execution
CompletionCandidate may request verification but cannot mark work complete
WaitCandidate requires a typed WakeCondition admitted outside free-form model text
human preemption or child failure re-enters exact predecessor identity and never blind-replays an effect
logical GRID cell count does not imply equal physical model concurrency
non_goals: do not create a second persistent agent identity per GRID cell
do not create one UnifiedDB authority per worker
do not treat local monologue text as canonical memory
do not equate native child spawn with cognitive authority

hypothesis.statement: AgentZero's one-shot, exact-reentry local deliberation envelope can improve GRID reliability if lifted from session scope to immutable workpackage/invocation scope while preserving deterministic arbitration.
hypothesis.counterhypothesis: The envelope's serialization and hook-mediated roundtrip may impose enough latency and coordination overhead that parallel GRID cognition loses more throughput than it gains in causal integrity.
hypothesis.falsifier: On the same fixed workpackage suite, compare workpackage-scoped GRIDLocalDeliberation with exact binding against a minimally bound parallel candidate baseline. Reject the hypothesis if exact binding fails to reduce identity/replay/completion errors while its latency/throughput cost exceeds the declared acceptance envelope.

triggerword4_feed: Keep the deterministic goal/step/generation envelope as a donor principle.
Do not freeze a session-global one-dispatch worker ABI for GRID; bind dispatch/child/tool identity per workpackage and invocation.
Keep CompletionCandidate non-authoritative and require independent typed evidence.
Implement typed WaitCandidate -> WakeCondition admission before exposing WAIT to model cognition.
Use the already-defined WorkExecutionBinding successor as the identity spine between native child lifecycle and this deliberation loop.
